body:
shouldn't this be @testing-library/jest-dom ?
It has been moved apparently: https://www.npmjs.com/package/jest-dom
Nice catch. Apparently their documentation is not up to date yet https://testing-library.com/docs/ecosystem-jest-dom

It could be nice to snapshot the calls to `.search` during each interaction.
One of the issues we had with the hierarchicalMenu is that it triggered too many requests

Adding an assertion with the number of requests (i.e. how many times the `searchClient.search()` method was called) might make more sense than snapshotting its calls. In the end, this testing strategy is about what is the state of the app at each step, not necessarily how we got there (this can be considered as an implementation detail). Keeping track of the number of requests can still be an important metric because it has a business impact and should be considered as a feature.
We don't want to use `search.started` because it's an internal.

It seems publicly exposed, but yes it is not documented :neutral_face: 

Also while making the change to use `search.started` I found an issue in `connectBreadcrumb`. If you do not provide an `unmountFn` during widget creation then `search.dispose()` crashes (no default value).

@yannickcr Some connectors still don't provide a default value for the unmount function. This is known but we haven't fixed that yet.

Regarding `search.started`, I don't think we should use it because it is not supposed to be exposed. This is an internal variable accessible because we use a class for `InstantSearch` and we store `started` on `this`. If we were to refactor this class to a function or even rename `started`, this will fail. I believe we should _strictly_ restrict ourselves to the public API with this move.
Agree to restrict ourselves to the public API
